# Message Scroller

Provides transcript anchoring, live-edge following, history restoration, and message navigation.

## Contents

- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Anchoring turns](#anchoring-turns)
- [Following the live edge](#following-the-live-edge)
- [Opening threads and loading history](#opening-threads-and-loading-history)
- [Commands and visibility](#commands-and-visibility)
- [Accessibility](#accessibility)
- [State ownership](#state-ownership)

## Installation

Add Message Scroller from the configured StackTrace registry.

```shell
npx shadcn-vue@latest add @stacktrace/message-scroller
```

## Usage

Wrap a height-constrained transcript in `MessageScrollerProvider`. The viewport is the native scroll region, the content is an accessible log, and every item may provide a stable `message-id`. Scroll the example to see the directional buttons appear only when more content exists.

**Message Scroller example**

```vue
<template>
  <MessageScrollerProvider default-scroll-position="start">
    <div class="h-96 w-full max-w-md overflow-hidden rounded-xl border bg-background">
      <MessageScroller>
        <MessageScrollerViewport>
          <MessageScrollerContent class="gap-6 p-4">
            <MessageScrollerItem
              v-for="message in messages"
              :key="message.id"
              :message-id="message.id"
              :scroll-anchor="message.align === 'end'"
            >
              <Message :align="message.align">
                <MessageContent>
                  <MessageHeader>{{ message.sender }}</MessageHeader>
                  <Bubble :variant="message.variant">
                    <BubbleContent>{{ message.text }}</BubbleContent>
                  </Bubble>
                </MessageContent>
              </Message>
            </MessageScrollerItem>
          </MessageScrollerContent>
        </MessageScrollerViewport>
        <MessageScrollerButton direction="start" />
        <MessageScrollerButton direction="end" />
      </MessageScroller>
    </div>
  </MessageScrollerProvider>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { Bubble, BubbleContent } from '@/Components/Bubble'
import { Message, MessageContent, MessageHeader } from '@/Components/Message'
import {
  MessageScroller,
  MessageScrollerButton,
  MessageScrollerContent,
  MessageScrollerItem,
  MessageScrollerProvider,
  MessageScrollerViewport,
} from '@/Components/MessageScroller'

const messages = [
  { id: 'm1', sender: 'You', align: 'end', variant: 'default', text: 'Can we keep new replies in view while they stream?' },
  { id: 'm2', sender: 'StackTrace', align: 'start', variant: 'muted', text: 'Yes. Enable auto-scroll and the viewport follows only while the reader remains at the live edge.' },
  { id: 'm3', sender: 'You', align: 'end', variant: 'default', text: 'What happens if I scroll up to read an earlier answer?' },
  { id: 'm4', sender: 'StackTrace', align: 'start', variant: 'muted', text: 'The scroller releases the live edge and preserves your position.' },
  { id: 'm5', sender: 'You', align: 'end', variant: 'default', text: 'Can I jump back to the latest message?' },
  { id: 'm6', sender: 'StackTrace', align: 'start', variant: 'muted', text: 'Use MessageScrollerButton. It appears only when more content exists in that direction.' },
] as const
</script>
```

## Anchoring turns

Set `scroll-anchor` on the row that starts a meaningful turn, commonly the user's message. When a new anchor arrives it settles near the top while `scroll-previous-item-peek` keeps part of the prior context visible. Anchors may also be system markers or handoff events; they are not tied to a message role.

## Following the live edge

Enable `auto-scroll` to follow a streamed reply while the reader remains at the bottom. Wheel, touch, keyboard, or scrollbar movement away from the live edge releases the viewport so incoming content does not pull the reader away from earlier messages. `MessageScrollerButton` returns to either edge and becomes inert when that edge is already visible.

## Opening threads and loading history

`default-scroll-position="last-anchor"` opens a saved thread at its latest meaningful turn; use `start` or `end` when that better matches the feature. The viewport preserves the visible row when earlier messages are prepended unless `preserve-scroll-on-prepend` is disabled.

## Commands and visibility

`useMessageScroller` exposes commands for scrolling to the start, end, or a stable message id. Use `useMessageScrollerVisibility` for the current anchor and visible ids, and `useMessageScrollerScrollable` when a custom control needs to know which edges remain reachable.

```ts
import { useMessageScroller } from '@/Components/MessageScroller'

const { scrollToMessage, scrollToEnd, scrollToStart } = useMessageScroller()

scrollToMessage('message-42', { align: 'center', behavior: 'smooth' })
```

## Accessibility

The viewport renders a focusable region labeled “Messages,” and the content uses `role="log"` with additions announced. Keep message text and controls semantically complete, preserve stable ids, and avoid animating item height, margin, or padding because layout animation can conflict with scroll anchoring.

## State ownership

Message Scroller owns scroll behavior only. It does not fetch history, store messages, stream model output, or choose turn boundaries. Those decisions remain in the conversation feature and are expressed through items, ids, anchors, and provider props.

Hosted documentation: [Message Scroller](https://ui.stacktrace.sk/docs/components/message-scroller)
